note:
The CAUCASIAN AMERICAN-AND-EUROPEAN selfie wave for the three clinical-result blocks on /pages/acetyl-hexapeptide-8-research. Malcolm, 2026-08-26: same background principle as the previous wave, but with Caucasian American and European amateur models.

CASTING NARROWS AGAIN, AND THE RECORD OF WHY MATTERS BECAUSE IT HAS MOVED TWICE. On 2026-08-25 the instruction was Caucasian only. On 2026-08-26 it broadened to blondes, redheads and other ethnic European and American backgrounds, and the four ethnicity bans were removed from the negative list to let that happen. It now narrows back to Caucasian, split deliberately between AMERICAN and EUROPEAN origins. The nine: Midwest American dishwater blonde; Irish-American faded auburn, densely freckled; Southern American mid-brown brunette with real sun weathering; Italian-American near-black brunette; Danish pale ash-blonde; Irish coppery red; French chestnut brunette greying at the temples; Polish ash-blonde with broad cheekbones; Greek almost-black brunette. Four brunettes, three blondes, two red - the hair range Malcolm asked for in the previous round is preserved inside the narrower casting.

A light negative guard is restored, but the ethnicity is stated POSITIVELY and per slot in the prompt body, which has consistently held better than a ban list. The lesson from removing those bans still stands: a stale negative is the hardest kind of instruction to notice, because nobody reads the negative list when the prompt looks right.

⚠️ f3'S MAGNITUDE IS CAPPED THIS ROUND, ON EVIDENCE FROM THE LAST ONE. Two f3 candidates in the brunette wave showed a visibly smoother forehead in the after panel - more change than a 14.6% fine-wrinkle improvement can support. On f1 (48.9%) and f2 (~30%) that degree of softening is defensible; on f3 it is not, and an overstated small finding is exactly the kind of thing that turns an illustration into a claim. f3's after-text now states that the two deeper creases are COMPLETELY UNCHANGED, that the forehead must not read smoother overall, that the skin must not look refreshed, and that a viewer should have to compare carefully to see it - and should then be able to. The visible-improvement floor and this ceiling are both live on f3 and they are deliberately narrow.

BACKGROUND PRINCIPLE UNCHANGED FROM THE PREVIOUS WAVE, AND IT IS A CAUSAL FIX RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE. Each room carries ONE soft unidentifiable element - a doorframe edge, the corner of two walls, a blurred chair back, an unreadable picture frame, a switched-off lampshade, a plain curtain fall, a skirting line, a coat on a hook, an empty shelf line, the side of an empty bookcase - thrown well out of focus. When the previous-but-one wave used entirely bare walls, nbp_flash put a phone back in frame on two slots after several clean rounds; the most likely cause is that an empty edge left nothing for the model to place there, so it supplied the object the scene implies. Giving it one legitimate thing to put at the edge fixed it, and the brunette wave came back with no phone or hand anywhere.

AGE STAYS AT FORTY-FIVE TO FIFTY-FIVE, as set in the previous round: lines WELL ESTABLISHED and more numerous than at forty, grey at the parting and temples normal and expected, but no deep folds, heavy jowls or badly slack neck of a woman in her sixties.

CASTING RANGE IS KEPT AS APPROVED: Scandinavian pale ash-blonde; Irish coppery red, densely freckled; southern Italian olive; Polish ash-blonde with broad cheekbones; African-American deep brown with coiled hair; Mexican-American warm tan-brown; mixed-race American golden-brown with curls; central European dark curly going grey; north of England strawberry-blonde and ruddy - all shifted into the new age band.

⚠️ DEEPER COMPLEXIONS KEEP THEIR OWN LIGHTING NOTE. An expression line on deep brown skin reads far less by shadow and much more by how a specular highlight breaks along it, and engines left unguided render dark skin grey and ashy. The relevant slots state that the skin stays WARM and luminous with its own undertones and that the sidelight picks out a sheen along the cheekbone. `no ashy grey skin, no grey cast on dark skin, no desaturated skin` are negated, and `no change of skin colour between the panels, no lighter skin in the right panel` guard the after-panel against lightening her - the same class of dishonesty as making her younger.

CARRIED FORWARD: nine slots so each image gets its own prompt; a very close crop cutting through the top of the forehead and just below the chin; no hand, arm or phone in frame; bright but DIRECTIONAL sidelight so lines actually cast; the visible-improvement floor; the honesty device that no line may disappear; and NO BAKED-IN TEXT, because Langify translates page content and cannot touch pixels.

nbp_pro remains excluded on evidence (seven waves of invented captions). Luma refuses this brief family with HTTP 422. CLASS B, 2048x2048.

slots.title: f1 · 48.9% — a white AMERICAN woman, rooms 1+2
slots.prompt:
Two ordinary phone selfies of THE SAME WOMAN, taken WEEKS APART at home, placed side by side to fill one square frame edge to edge: TWO PANELS OF EXACTLY EQUAL WIDTH meeting at one crisp vertical edge precisely at the centre. Each panel is a tall portrait. The left panel is the earlier one, the right panel is the later one.

Her expression is flat and unposed on both days, mouth closed, not smiling.

THESE ARE TWO SEPARATE OCCASIONS, NOT TWO COPIES OF ONE FRAME. Everything that identifies her stays the same, and everything a different day would change is different.

UNMISTAKABLY THE SAME WOMAN: the same face shape and jawline, the same nose, the same eye colour, the same skin colour, the same brow shape, the same hair colour and cut, and her moles and freckles in the same places.

THE TWO PLACES ARE DIFFERENT ROOMS. On the earlier day she is in an ordinary room with a WARM WHITE wall behind her and, far out of focus at one edge, the soft vertical edge of a doorframe; daylight arriving from her left. On the later day she is in an ordinary room with a PALE GREY wall behind her and, well out of focus, the faint corner where two walls meet; brighter daylight arriving from her right. Two plainly different neutral interiors - a different wall colour and a different light direction each time. NOTHING IS IN VIEW BEHIND HER BUT THE PAINTED WALL: no furniture, no pictures, no shelves, no appliances, no doorway, no window in shot, no clutter and no objects of any kind. The wall is softly out of focus and completely bare.

ALSO DIFFERENT BETWEEN THE TWO DAYS: the angle she holds the phone at and the camera height; where her eyes go on the screen; a completely different everyday garment; and her hair, the same cut but unstyled and falling differently.

IT MUST BE OBVIOUS AT A GLANCE THAT SHE TOOK THIS HERSELF - BUT THE PHONE AND HER HANDS ARE NEVER IN THE PICTURE. This is the view THROUGH the front camera of the phone she is holding, so the hand holding it cannot appear in its own frame, and neither can the phone. NO HAND, NO FINGERS, NO ARM, NO ELBOW, NO PHONE, NO PHONE CASE, NO MIRROR AND NO REFLECTION anywhere in either panel.

THE PHONE IS HELD RIGHT UP CLOSE AND HER FACE COMPLETELY FILLS THE PANEL. The frame cuts across her forehead just below the hairline at the top and at the point of her chin at the bottom, and her cheeks run all the way to both edges of the panel and are slightly cut off by them. Her whole forehead, both eyes and the whole mouth are still in view - the eye corners and the forehead lines are the point of the picture and must not be cropped away - but there is essentially no space left around her face. Only narrow slivers of the room show past her at the very edges. Because the lens is this close it visibly distorts: her nose and chin read large, her forehead looms, and the sides of her head fall away sharply.

The other tells are in the camera, not her limbs: the angle is NOT eye level, she is watching her own face on the screen so her gaze sits slightly off the lens, the frame is a few degrees crooked and off-centre, and it is a phone file - imperfect focus, noise in the shadows, indoor white balance a little wrong.

She is a white AMERICAN woman of about fifty from the Midwest, with dull dishwater-blonde hair pulled back into a clip and a few greys at the parting, fair skin, pale blue eyes, sparse fair brows, and a faintly ruddy unevenness across the cheeks. She wears no makeup at all, her brows are natural and unshaped, and her hair is unstyled. She is an ordinary person, not a model, and neither picture makes any attempt to flatter her.

SHE IS BETWEEN FORTY-FIVE AND FIFTY-FIVE AND THAT GOVERNS WHAT HER SKIN CAN HONESTLY LOOK LIKE. Her expression lines are WELL ESTABLISHED - they stay put with her face at rest, hold a real shadow, and there are more of them than a woman of forty would have. But she is not elderly: no deep folds of a woman in her sixties or seventies, no heavy jowls, no badly slack neck. Some grey at the parting and temples is right and expected at this age.

THE ONE THING THAT MUST BE TRUE: the number and position of the lines is the same in both panels and NOT ONE HAS DISAPPEARED. Her moles, freckles and marks are all still there in the same places. What has changed is only HOW DEEP the lines are. She has not been made younger, slimmer, prettier, lighter-skinned or better groomed.

THERE MUST BE A VISIBLE IMPROVEMENT IN THE LATER PICTURE. This is the entire purpose of the pair. Someone comparing the two panels must be able to SEE that the lines are softer in the later one and point to which ones. TWO PANELS THAT LOOK THE SAME ARE A COMPLETE FAILURE. It is still a believable improvement and not a transformation: the same lines are all present, in the same places, just less deeply cut. Nothing else about her improves.

BOTH PICTURES ARE BRIGHT AND WELL EXPOSED, AND IN BOTH THE DAYLIGHT ARRIVES FROM ONE SIDE. This matters more than anything else about the lighting: flat frontal light flatters skin and hides what the picture exists to show, while light coming across her face rakes over the surface so every line casts its own small shadow. So - bright, clean, no dark room, no murk, no heavy shadow swallowing half the face, no flash - but definitely DIRECTIONAL, with a clear light side and a softer shaded side. The direction and quality differ between the two days; the sidelit quality does not.

THE SKIN MUST HOLD UP AS REAL AND UNFLATTERED, and at this crop it is nearly the whole picture. Pores are clearly visible and vary in size and density by zone - open across the nose and inner cheeks, finer at the temples and jaw - several individually larger than their neighbours. Pigmentation is uneven and asymmetric, never mirrored from one side of the face to the other. Fine vellus hairs catch the sidelight along the jaw and upper lip. The skin is a little greasy across the nose and forehead and drier at the outer cheeks. No makeup on either day, so her lips, lashes and brows are their own natural colour.

ON THE EARLIER DAY, in the LEFT panel, her expression lines are established and plainly visible with her face at rest: a fan of four creases at the outer corner of each eye, three horizontal lines across the forehead, a pair of short vertical creases between the brows, and a line beginning to run down from each side of the nose. In the sidelight each holds a clear shadow along its length.

ON THE LATER DAY, in the RIGHT panel, EVERY ONE OF THOSE LINES IS STILL THERE, IN THE SAME PLACES AND THE SAME NUMBER, AND NOT ONE HAS DISAPPEARED - but each is about HALF as deep, holding a lighter and shorter shadow, so the difference is plain when the halves are compared. Her moles, freckles and skin tone are exactly as they were.

A snapshot off a phone, not a photograph - slightly soft, slightly noisy, honest and completely unretouched.
